name: Aubrey Yates
life: “I still remember stripes sewn slightly differently for each hotel balcony.” On Friday, near Juniper Street, Aubrey knows which of the west-side porches has a seat in the shade.
voice: I manage the hotel that owns the stripes. I took the patched one to lunch and liked the shade better.
appearance: Aubrey has short copper curls, a broad nose and a deep dimple on one cheek, and a favorite piece of clothing, a cream pullover. It usually goes with a folded shopping list secured by a miniature clip. When somebody else has the floor, Aubrey holds eye contact until the other person has finished.
personality: Aubrey treats keeping somebody waiting as a serious discourtesy. This can turn a helpful person into an impatient one when everybody else needs a slower conversation.
agenda: To return the hotel's stripes to the hire stand.
family: Ellen Boone is Aubrey’s stepsibling. Aubrey picks the meeting place. Ellen sets the time to leave. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *Land without cranes*, Ellen says, “I am taking an office course in secret. I want the conversion to include a room where I could actually learn.”
connections: Audrey Kahn (boardwalk supplier). They trace a striped hotel parasol from the hire stand to the chess game.

reactions.situation: A hotel worker asks to throw the patched umbrella away
reactions.response: Aubrey puts the patched umbrella aside until the owner can explain the repair.

reactions.situation: A street musician can't finish a familiar song
reactions.response: Aubrey keeps listening through the pause and lets the musician choose the next note.

reactions.situation: If a frightened person needs longer
reactions.response: Aubrey changes the plan openly and takes responsibility for the delay.
